# ADR-013: Review queue frontend: separate SPA on REST endpoints

**Status**: superseded by ADR-0025 (2026-10-04: pages generated by the server with Qute and htmx).
Accepted on 2026-07-16. Note of 2026-09-27: the `orpheus-web` module, left empty, was removed; the
review interface was to be redesigned and this decision revisited then.

## Context

The review queue (`/review`, SPEC.md section 5) is a supporting web interface, not Orpheus's primary
interface: that is the CLI (ADR-012). An interactive experience is still needed to browse, confirm,
replace or reject review items.

## Decision

A separate single-page application (SPA), consuming REST endpoints exposed by Quarkus (RESTEasy
Reactive) in the same artifact, consistent with the "single process for CLI and web UI" topology
already fixed in ADR-007. Reason: decoupling, so that the frontend does not depend on server-side
details and the domain logic exposed through REST stays the same surface, testable independently of
the UI.

## Consequences

The concrete SPA framework or library remains an open implementation choice, not necessarily an ADR
of its own given the small surface of the web UI (a few pages, a single user): to be evaluated at
scaffolding time, not as an architectural decision.
